comments.author: throw0101d
comments.story: Using street lamps as EV chargers
comments.why: Ubitricity system for charging EVs from lamp posts
comments.text: Robert Llewellyn (previously of Red Dwarf fame) covered this idea eight years ago (July 2017) on his 'electrify' channel: > The simple and very commonplace lamp post will soon become a ubiquitous charge point for electric cars. They charge at about 5 kW, or 16 amps, not super fast but overnight charging is all most drivers need. Ubitricity is a German based company who've come up with a simple, cheap to install and well managed system for more people on more streets to adopt electric cars. * [VIDEO] See also pop-up chargers from six years ago: * [LINK]

comments.text: Fully Charged , based out of the UK, had episodes on street lamp plugs, and pop-up chargers: * [VIDEO] * [LINK] Each area/street will probably have to examined individually to find the right solution for it.

comments.author: throw0101a
comments.story: Electric vehicles close to ‘tipping point’ of mass adoption
comments.why: Street lamp charging option for garage orphans
comments.text: > The number of people in the UK and Ireland that have to park overnight on the street is way too high to start banning ICE vehicles within the next decade. You're not wrong (and I too am a "garage orphan"—neither a garage or even a driveway), but there are some options being developed. The YT channel Fully Charged featured two a while back: * Street lamps: [VIDEO] * Pop-up charger: [LINK] I'm a bit skeptical.

comments.author: throw0101a
comments.story: Electric vehicles close to ‘tipping point’ of mass adoption
comments.text: Reasonable concern, though: 1. If every car has one, they become a commodity, so how much value will they actually end up having? 2. There are locking cables available: * [VIDEO]

comments.author: throw0101a
comments.story: Where will ‘garage orphans’ charge electric cars?
comments.why: Episode on charging from street lamp posts
comments.text: Fully Charged did an episode on this: * [VIDEO] However, in many cities the posts are not in the sidewalk, but on people's properties, so as to allow clearer pedestrian paths. This is generally true in Toronto (where the story is written), especially on residential side-streets.

comments.author: throw0101a
comments.story: Where will ‘garage orphans’ charge electric cars?
comments.why: Episode on Ubitricity lamp post charging
comments.text: Fully Charged had an episode on Ubitricity: * [VIDEO] This mostly works if the posts are closer to the curb, but in some places they are on people's front lawns so the sidewalks are completely clear.
